title: The SEC's Short-Sale Experiment: Evidence on Causal Channels and Reassessment of Indirect Effects
authors: Bernard S. Black; Hemang Desai; Katherine Litvak; Woongsun Yoo; Jeff Jiewei Yu
eligible_reason: Reg SHO pilot: randomized removal of short-sale restrictions for one third of Russell 3000 firms, all starting on the same date (May 2005) and ending for everyone in 2007; a single cohort, not staggered adoption (same ruling as mnsc.2023.4783). Table 2 (monthly short interest): areg shortint_pct pre_launch_pilot experiment_pilot pre_launch_dummy experiment_dummy i.ym, absorb(gvkey), with pre-launch and experiment windows at common calendar months. Tables 4-7 (annual reassessments of FHK, GMW, HHZ, LLS): xtreg y pilot_during pilot_post i.fyear, fe, where DURING/POST are defined by fiscal-year-end month in fixed calendar windows (Oct 2005-Dec 2007, from Jan 2008), so differences in onset across firms come only from fiscal-year ends (PROTOCOL section 6: single-policy design). Most columns carry both during and post pilot regressors; some add time-varying firm controls or Tobin's q interactions.
design_notes: Stata areg/xtreg with firm and month (or fiscal-year) FE, cluster by firm. Table 3 (causal channels: returns, managerial fear) via log/figure workbook. Figures 7-8 in R plot t-statistics across specification choices.
data_files_note: Table-level analysis files shipped (derived from Compustat/CRSP/short-interest data).
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract. Single-date Reg SHO experiment; consistent with the mnsc.2023.4783 ruling.
